title: Robot data startup Mecka AI nabs $60M from Sequoia
source_used: TechCrunch (full text read; page carries Disrupt ad copy, not used)
key_facts: Mecka AI, founded in 2024, announced a $60 million Series B round led by Sequoia, with Nvidia, Microsoft's venture fund M12 and others.
Mecka collects and analyses human motion data to train humanoid and other robots.
Mecka pays people to record everyday tasks, such as making coffee or fixing cars, while wearing body sensors and using smartphones.
TechCrunch had reported earlier that the startup was nearing a round at a $500 million valuation; this article does not confirm the valuation.
Peers named: XDOF (in talks at a $1.2 billion valuation, per TechCrunch's earlier reporting); Scale AI and Micro1 are expanding into robotics.
The article gives no revenue or results.
